A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LuxRemix with the same authors, research objective and pipeline. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete supplementary material support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original quantitative experiments on 30 held-out synthetic scenes in Tables 1–2, alongside qualitative lighting-editing results and ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds quantitative results on ten paired real-world LightLab examples in Table 4 and a qualitative consistency comparison.

M1.justification: The single-view decomposition, multi-view harmonization, HDR reconstruction and Gaussian lighting procedures remain unchanged, including the appendix training objectives. The newly stated coefficient initialization provides implementation detail without establishing a changed method.

E1.justification: LightLab real-world editing examples already appear in v1 Figure 8. V2 adds quantitative evaluation within that coverage and another synthetic indoor consistency example, without introducing a distinct dataset domain or task requirement.

E2.justification: Table 4 quantifies comparisons with ScribbleLight, Qwen-Image and LightLab, the same comparators already used in Figure 8. Existing synthetic comparison methods, model variants and other qualitative comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: New Section 8.3 specifies evaluation on ten paired LightLab examples, tuning each method's light-editing parameters to best match the target before reporting PSNR, SSIM and LPIPS. The existing 30-scene synthetic protocol and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Figure 13 and Section 8.4 visually compare independent LuxRemix-SV editing with LuxRemix-MV harmonization, illustrating cross-view lighting and shadow inconsistencies. This supplements the existing Table 2 ablation; earlier failure cases and other analyses remain.

E5.justification: The qualitative seed-dependence example in Figure 14 is retained. V2 adds no repeated-run counts, uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 retain their numerical results. New Table 4 reports LuxRemix at 20.93/0.771/0.168 versus LightLab at 21.80/0.791/0.144 for PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS, placing LightLab ahead on all three metrics. Figure 13 adds qualitative consistency results; these are additional findings, not same-setting performance improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The lighting decomposition equation, appendix light-composition definitions and optimization losses in Equations 1–5 are retained. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The fourth introductory contribution now explicitly states that the synthetic dataset is being publicly released. The abstract, principal methodological contributions and concluding claims about controllable multi-view relighting otherwise retain their scope.

C2.justification: New Section 8.3 acknowledges LightLab's stronger real-world scores while interpreting LuxRemix as competitive despite synthetic-only training. The existing limitations concerning outdoor or dynamic scenes, conical light-spread bias and unsupported HDRI editing remain.

D1.justification: V2 newly documents SfM pose estimation, typically 32–96 real-scene input images, and Gaussian coefficient initialization from harmonization outputs. It announces dataset release and revises Section 6's dataset description from 12,400 rooms and 4.5 TB to over 12,000 rooms and 9 TB; these disclosures do not establish changed training coverage.

R1.justification: Section 2.3 adds GaSLight for spatially varying HDR lighting. The optimizer citation changes from the Adam paper to Decoupled Weight Decay Regularization for the retained AdamW optimizer. Overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: V2 condenses portions of the introduction, related work and method explanations while retaining the main narrative structure. The supplement gains two evaluation subsections, and Figure 3's inconsistent 10,000-scene description becomes over 12,000.

P2.justification: V2 adds Table 4 and the consistency comparison in Figure 13, shortens several captions and adjusts display placement. V1's additional harmonization Figure 13 is retained as v2 Figure 15, and the failure-case figure remains Figure 14.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens the previously qualitative real-world evaluation with a paired quantitative comparison that transparently reports LightLab's lead. The new consistency illustration and implementation disclosures also improve clarity. These are limited gains: the real-world evaluation covers ten examples with target-specific parameter tuning, while the core method and existing quantitative evidence remain unchanged.
